Two-person infrared saunas here start at $1,999, and nearly every one runs on a standard 120V household outlet. This is the entry point to the category, and for most buyers it is the size that actually gets used.

Read the capacity claim carefully

Several cabins in this range are listed as "1-2 person". That is accurate and it is worth taking literally: two adults fit upright, seated, without much room between them. If you want to stretch out, or if two people will use it together regularly, look at the three-person cabins instead. The bench depth in the specification tells you more than the headline capacity does.

What you get at this price

Canadian hemlock is the standard wood at this size, with cedar appearing on a small number of units at a premium. Most cabins list chromotherapy lighting as fitted rather than as an upgrade. Heat runs at 120 to 140°F, so plan on 30 to 45 minute sessions rather than the 15 you would spend in a traditional room.

Standard delivery is free to the lower 48 with no minimum and is curbside drop-off — you move it inside and assemble it. Inside delivery to any room is $600, and $1,800 covers inside delivery plus unboxing and full assembly.

EMF tiers vary between manufacturers and are measured at different distances from the panel, so compare like with like: low EMF is roughly 5 to 10 mG, ultra low 3 to 5, and near zero 2 to 3. For larger cabins see indoor infrared saunas.
